categories.label: Self-KO
categories.description: The wild Pokémon faints itself by using the move. One use ends the encounter with nothing left to catch.

categories.label: Flee / battle-ending
categories.description: Moves that end a wild battle outright: the wild Pokémon teleports away, or scares or blows your Pokémon off. Whether they work depends on the generation and on the two Pokémon's levels.

categories.label: Delayed KO
categories.description: Effects that take the wild Pokémon, or the Pokémon you are battling with, out on a timer or on a trigger.

categories.label: Recoil
categories.description: The wild Pokémon damages itself whenever its attack connects. Recoil is always at least 1 HP, so a target left at 1 HP by False Swipe faints as soon as a recoil move lands. Wild Pokémon with Rock Head or Magic Guard take no recoil (Struggle excepted). In Legends: Arceus a strong-style recoil move costs more: 1/2 of the damage dealt for Double-Edge, Flare Blitz, Brave Bird, Wood Hammer, Volt Tackle, Wave Crash and Wild Charge, 3/4 for Head Smash.

categories.label: Crash damage
categories.description: The wild Pokémon hurts itself when the attack fails to land: on a miss, and in later generations also when you use Protect or your Pokémon is immune.

categories.label: HP cost
categories.description: Moves the wild Pokémon pays for with its own HP. Some refuse to work when the user cannot afford them; others (Ghost-type Curse, Mind Blown, Steel Beam, Chloroblast) will happily make the user faint.

categories.label: Self-confusion
categories.description: Rampage moves that leave the wild Pokémon confused afterwards. A confused Pokémon can hit itself, which is lethal once it has been weakened.

categories.label: Weather chip damage
categories.description: Weather the wild Pokémon summons that damages every non-immune Pokémon at the end of each turn. It only matters when the wild Pokémon itself is not immune, but then a target at 1 HP faints at the end of the turn.

categories.label: Friendly fire (multi-wild battles)
categories.description: Moves that hit every adjacent Pokémon, allies included. Only a risk when more than one wild Pokémon is on the field: wild Double Battles (Gen 4 partner areas, Gen 5 dark grass, BD/SP partner areas), Horde Encounters (Gen 6) and SOS Battles (Gen 7), where the shiny's partners can knock it out.

categories.label: Catcher threat
categories.description: Moves that do not hurt the target but stall or break a catching setup: trapping your Pokémon, making the target impossible to aim at, or blocking your status moves.

categories.label: Wildcard
categories.description: Moves that can turn into any other move, including the ones in the categories above.

moves.name: Self-Destruct
moves.reason: The wild Pokémon faints itself the moment it uses the move, leaving nothing to catch.
moves.detail: The user always faints: from Gen 2 on even if the move misses, is blocked by Protect, hits a Substitute or your Pokémon is a Ghost-type (in the Gen 1 handheld games it survives only if the blast breaks a Substitute). Gen 4 only: fails without fainting if no target is left. It hits every adjacent Pokémon, so in horde, SOS and double wild battles a partner's blast can also KO the shiny. Fails, with the user unharmed, while any Pokémon with Damp is on the field. Sturdy, Focus Sash and Focus Band do not save the user. Legends: Arceus exception: the user does not faint but loses 80% of its max HP as recoil (70% agile style, 90% strong style), and nothing happens if the move misses or the target is immune.
moves.counter: Lead with a Damp Pokémon: the move fails and the user survives. A Ghost-type lead does NOT save it. Without Damp, open with a Quick Ball or put it to sleep before it gets a turn.

moves.name: Explosion
moves.reason: The wild Pokémon faints itself the moment it uses the move, leaving nothing to catch.
moves.detail: The user always faints: from Gen 2 on even if the move misses, is blocked by Protect, hits a Substitute or your Pokémon is a Ghost-type (in the Gen 1 handheld games it survives only if the blast breaks a Substitute). Gen 4 only: fails without fainting if no target is left. It hits every adjacent Pokémon, so in horde, SOS and double wild battles a partner's blast can also KO the shiny. Fails, with the user unharmed, while any Pokémon with Damp is on the field. Sturdy, Focus Sash and Focus Band do not save the user.
moves.counter: Lead with a Damp Pokémon: the move fails and the user survives. A Ghost-type lead does NOT save it. Without Damp, open with a Quick Ball or put it to sleep before it gets a turn.

moves.name: Misty Explosion
moves.reason: The wild Pokémon faints itself the moment it uses the move, leaving nothing to catch.
moves.detail: Gen 8+ special Fairy-type counterpart of Explosion: the user always faints. Base power 100, or 150 on Misty Terrain if the user is grounded; hits every adjacent Pokémon. Fails without the user fainting if a Pokémon with Damp is on the field. Cannot be selected in Brilliant Diamond / Shining Pearl.
moves.counter: Lead with a Damp Pokémon, or catch it or put it to sleep before it gets a turn.

moves.name: Memento
moves.reason: The wild Pokémon faints itself in order to cut your Pokémon's Attack and Special Attack by two stages each.
moves.detail: Gen 3-4: the user faints even when Memento is blocked by Protect or a Substitute or cannot lower the stats (Gen 4: even on a miss; Gen 3: it survives only if both of the target's stats are already at -6). Gen 5+: the user does NOT faint if Memento misses or is blocked by Protect or a Substitute, but still faints if it hits and the stats simply cannot drop (for example Clear Body).
moves.counter: Taunt stops it (Memento is a status move). From Gen 5 a Substitute or a well-timed Protect makes it fail without the user fainting. Otherwise catch it or put it to sleep before it gets a turn.

moves.name: Final Gambit
moves.reason: The wild Pokémon faints itself to deal damage equal to its remaining HP.
moves.detail: The user faints whenever the move hits. If it misses, is blocked by Protect, or the target is immune (Ghost-type), the move fails and the user does not faint. Sturdy, Focus Sash and Focus Band do not save the user.
moves.counter: Lead with a Ghost-type (immune, so the move fails and the user survives) or use Protect on the turn it attacks.

moves.name: Teleport
moves.reason: A wild Pokémon that uses Teleport flees and the battle ends immediately.
moves.detail: Gen 1: flees; only when its level is lower than your active Pokémon's can it fail, with chance floor(yourLevel / 4) / (yourLevel + wildLevel + 1), roughly 10-25%. Gen 2: always succeeds for wild Pokémon (the level check is skipped by a bug) unless it is trapped by Mean Look or Spider Web; it fails in scripted encounters such as the Red Gyarados. Gen 3-7: always succeeds in a single wild battle unless the user is trapped by a move (Mean Look, Block, Spider Web, binding moves) or an Ability (Shadow Tag, Arena Trap); it fails in wild battles that are not Single Battles. Gen 8+ (Sword/Shield, BD/SP, Scarlet/Violet): priority -6, and it succeeds even when the user is trapped. Legends: Arceus uses its own action-order system instead of priority, but its move description also says a wild user flees. Legends: Z-A reworks the move for real-time battles (description: the user teleports back to its Trainer).
moves.counter: Gen 3-7: lead with Shadow Tag or Arena Trap (Arena Trap does not hold Flying-types or Levitate users), or use Mean Look / Block. Gen 2: Mean Look or Spider Web. Any generation: put it to sleep or Taunt it (Gen 3+, Teleport is a status move); from Gen 4 a Quick Ball on turn one is the simplest answer. Gen 8+: trapping no longer works, but Teleport moves last, so you always get one action first.

moves.name: Roar
moves.reason: Used by a wild Pokémon in a one-on-one wild battle, Roar scares your Pokémon off and ends the battle on the spot.
moves.detail: Gen 1-2: ends the wild battle; only when the wild Pokémon's level is lower than your Pokémon's can it fail, with chance floor(yourLevel / 4) / (yourLevel + wildLevel + 1), roughly 10-25%. Gen 3-4: same level rule with a slightly different roll (it fails when floor(X * (yourLevel + wildLevel) / 256) + 1 <= floor(yourLevel / 4) for a random X from 0 to 255); priority -6; fails against Soundproof, Suction Cups and Ingrain. Gen 5+: always fails if the wild Pokémon's level is lower than your Pokémon's, otherwise it ends the battle; if several wild Pokémon are (or were) in the battle it drags out a random member of your party instead. Gen 6+: cannot miss and goes through Protect. Legends: Z-A reworks the move for real-time battles (description: it drives targets back a good distance).
moves.counter: Gen 5+: lead with a Pokémon at least one level above the target and Roar always fails. Gen 3+: a Soundproof or Suction Cups lead (or Ingrain) blocks it at any level. From Gen 3 it has -6 priority, so you always act first each turn.

moves.name: Whirlwind
moves.reason: Used by a wild Pokémon in a one-on-one wild battle, Whirlwind blows your Pokémon away and ends the battle on the spot.
moves.detail: Gen 1-2: ends the wild battle (85% accuracy in Gen 1, 100% from Gen 2); only when the wild Pokémon's level is lower than your Pokémon's can it fail, with chance floor(yourLevel / 4) / (yourLevel + wildLevel + 1), roughly 10-25%. Gen 3-4: same level rule with a slightly different roll (it fails when floor(X * (yourLevel + wildLevel) / 256) + 1 <= floor(yourLevel / 4) for a random X from 0 to 255); priority -6; fails against Suction Cups and Ingrain. Gen 5+: always fails if the wild Pokémon's level is lower than your Pokémon's, otherwise it ends the battle; if several wild Pokémon are (or were) in the battle it drags out a random member of your party instead. Gen 6+: cannot miss and goes through Protect. Legends: Z-A reworks the move for real-time battles (description: it drives targets back a good distance). Unlike Roar it is not sound-based, so Soundproof does not help.
moves.counter: Gen 5+: lead with a Pokémon at least one level above the target and Whirlwind always fails. Gen 3+: a Suction Cups lead (or Ingrain) blocks it at any level. From Gen 3 it has -6 priority, so you always act first each turn.

moves.name: Dragon Tail
moves.reason: If it hits while the wild Pokémon's level is equal to or higher than your Pokémon's, the one-on-one wild battle ends.
moves.detail: Damaging move with -6 priority and 90% accuracy. In a single wild battle it ends the battle when the user's level is equal to or greater than the target's; with several wild Pokémon it forces your switch instead. It does not end the battle if your Pokémon has Suction Cups, is rooted by Ingrain, is behind a Substitute, or is immune to the hit (Fairy-types from Gen 6).
moves.counter: Lead with a Pokémon above the target's level, a Fairy-type (Gen 6+) or a Suction Cups Pokémon, or keep a Substitute up.

moves.name: Circle Throw
moves.reason: If it hits while the wild Pokémon's level is equal to or higher than your Pokémon's, the one-on-one wild battle ends.
moves.detail: Damaging move with -6 priority and 90% accuracy. In a single wild battle it ends the battle when the user's level is equal to or greater than the target's; with several wild Pokémon it forces your switch instead. It does not end the battle if your Pokémon has Suction Cups, is rooted by Ingrain, is behind a Substitute, or is immune to the hit (Ghost-types).
moves.counter: Lead with a Pokémon above the target's level, a Ghost-type or a Suction Cups Pokémon, or keep a Substitute up.

moves.name: Perish Song
moves.reason: Every Pokémon on the field, the wild singer included, faints when its perish count runs out, so the encounter is on a hard timer.
moves.detail: The perish count starts at 4 and drops by 1 at the end of every turn, including the turn the song is used; at 0 the Pokémon faints. That leaves you three more turns of actions. It cannot miss and ignores Protect and Substitute. Switching your Pokémon out clears its count; a wild Pokémon cannot switch, so it will faint. Soundproof Pokémon are immune (Gen 3-7: a Soundproof user is immune to its own song; Gen 8+: the user is always affected). In horde, SOS and double wild battles the other wild Pokémon get a count too.
moves.counter: Start throwing balls immediately and switch your own Pokémon out before its count reaches 0. Taunt (Gen 3+) or sleep stops the song from being sung at all. A Soundproof lead protects only itself, not the wild Pokémon.

moves.name: Destiny Bond
moves.reason: If you knock the wild Pokémon out while Destiny Bond is active your attacker faints with it, which can wreck a chain that relies on a single battler.
moves.detail: Active until the user's next move. It triggers only when the user faints from a direct attack; indirect damage (weather, Leech Seed, Future Sight) does not trigger it, and Focus Sash, Sturdy and Magic Guard do not save your Pokémon. Gen 7+: it always fails if it was used successfully on the previous turn. It never matters while you are only catching, since False Swipe cannot KO.
moves.counter: When chaining KOs, do not land the finishing hit on the turn after it uses Destiny Bond, or finish it with indirect damage.

moves.name: Take Down
moves.reason: The wild Pokémon takes recoil every time the attack connects and can knock itself out once weakened.
moves.detail: Recoil: 1/4 of the damage dealt, in every generation. 85% accuracy. No damage dealt means no recoil.
moves.counter: Lead with a Ghost-type (immune to Normal moves, so no damage and no recoil) or a bulky Rock- or Steel-type that takes little damage. Put it to sleep before using False Swipe, and never leave it at 1 HP while it can still attack.

moves.name: Double-Edge
moves.reason: The wild Pokémon takes heavy recoil every time the attack connects and can knock itself out once weakened.
moves.detail: Recoil: 1/3 of the damage dealt from Gen 3 on; 1/4 in Gen 1-2. 100% accuracy. No damage dealt means no recoil.
moves.counter: Lead with a Ghost-type (immune to Normal moves, so no damage and no recoil) or a bulky Rock- or Steel-type that takes little damage. Put it to sleep before using False Swipe, and never leave it at 1 HP while it can still attack.

moves.name: Submission
moves.reason: The wild Pokémon takes recoil every time the attack connects and can knock itself out once weakened.
moves.detail: Recoil: 1/4 of the damage dealt. 80% accuracy. Cannot be selected in Gen 9 (Scarlet/Violet).
moves.counter: Lead with a Ghost-type (immune to Fighting moves, so no damage and no recoil). Put it to sleep before using False Swipe, and never leave it at 1 HP while it can still attack.

moves.name: Volt Tackle
moves.reason: The wild Pokémon takes heavy recoil every time the attack connects and can knock itself out once weakened.
moves.detail: Recoil: 1/3 of the damage dealt. From Gen 4 it also has a 10% chance to paralyse your Pokémon.
moves.counter: Lead with a Ground-type (immune to Electric moves, so no damage and no recoil). Put it to sleep before using False Swipe, and never leave it at 1 HP while it can still attack.

moves.name: Flare Blitz
moves.reason: The wild Pokémon takes heavy recoil every time the attack connects and can knock itself out once weakened.
moves.detail: Recoil: 1/3 of the damage dealt. 10% chance to burn your Pokémon. Recoil scales with the damage dealt, so a frail or Fire-weak lead makes it worse.
moves.counter: Lead with a physically bulky Pokémon that resists Fire so the hit, and therefore the recoil, stays small. Put it to sleep before using False Swipe, and never leave it at 1 HP while it can still attack.

moves.name: Brave Bird
moves.reason: The wild Pokémon takes heavy recoil every time the attack connects and can knock itself out once weakened.
moves.detail: Recoil: 1/3 of the damage dealt. Recoil scales with the damage dealt, so a frail or Flying-weak lead makes it worse.
moves.counter: Lead with a physically bulky Pokémon that resists Flying (Rock, Steel or Electric) so the hit, and therefore the recoil, stays small. Put it to sleep before using False Swipe, and never leave it at 1 HP while it can still attack.

moves.name: Wood Hammer
moves.reason: The wild Pokémon takes heavy recoil every time the attack connects and can knock itself out once weakened.
moves.detail: Recoil: 1/3 of the damage dealt. Recoil scales with the damage dealt, so a frail or Grass-weak lead makes it worse.
moves.counter: Lead with a physically bulky Pokémon that resists Grass so the hit, and therefore the recoil, stays small. Put it to sleep before using False Swipe, and never leave it at 1 HP while it can still attack.

moves.name: Head Smash
moves.reason: The wild Pokémon takes the heaviest recoil of any standard move every time the attack connects and can knock itself out even from high HP.
moves.detail: Recoil: 1/2 of the damage dealt. Base power 150, 80% accuracy. Recoil scales with the damage dealt, so a frail or Rock-weak lead makes it worse.
moves.counter: Lead with a physically bulky Pokémon that resists Rock (Fighting, Ground or Steel) so the hit, and therefore the recoil, stays small. Put it to sleep before using False Swipe, and never leave it at 1 HP while it can still attack.

moves.name: Wild Charge
moves.reason: The wild Pokémon takes recoil every time the attack connects and can knock itself out once weakened.
moves.detail: Recoil: 1/4 of the damage dealt. 100% accuracy.
moves.counter: Lead with a Ground-type (immune to Electric moves, so no damage and no recoil). Put it to sleep before using False Swipe, and never leave it at 1 HP while it can still attack.

moves.name: Head Charge
moves.reason: The wild Pokémon takes recoil every time the attack connects and can knock itself out once weakened.
moves.detail: Recoil: 1/4 of the damage dealt. Cannot be selected in Brilliant Diamond / Shining Pearl or in Gen 9.
moves.counter: Lead with a Ghost-type (immune to Normal moves, so no damage and no recoil). Put it to sleep before using False Swipe, and never leave it at 1 HP while it can still attack.

moves.name: Wave Crash
moves.reason: The wild Pokémon takes heavy recoil every time the attack connects and can knock itself out once weakened.
moves.detail: Recoil: 1/3 of the damage dealt. Introduced in Legends: Arceus (base power 75 there, 120 from Gen 9).
moves.counter: Lead with a bulky Pokémon that resists Water so the hit, and therefore the recoil, stays small. Put it to sleep before using False Swipe, and never leave it at 1 HP while it can still attack.

moves.name: Struggle
moves.reason: A wild Pokémon with no usable move left is forced to Struggle and steadily knocks itself out.
moves.detail: Used automatically when every move is out of PP or blocked (Taunt, Torment, Disable, Imprison, Encore and similar). Recoil: 1/2 of the damage dealt in Gen 1; 1/4 of the damage dealt in Gen 2-3; 1/4 of the user's maximum HP from Gen 4 on, whatever it hits, so about four uses are fatal from full HP. Rock Head and Magic Guard do not prevent it. It never appears in a learnset: the risk is a long fight (SOS chains, many failed balls) or locking the target out of its moves.
moves.counter: Do not stall: wild Pokémon run out of PP in long fights. Never Taunt a target whose moves are all status moves. For long SOS chains, keep the caller's PP topped up (the usual setup is a Leppa Berry on the caller, often with Harvest).

moves.name: Jump Kick
moves.reason: When the kick fails to land the wild Pokémon crashes and damages itself, which is fatal once it is weakened.
moves.detail: 95% accuracy. Crash damage on a miss: Gen 1 - 1 HP. Gen 2 - 1/8 of the damage the kick would have dealt; Protect/Detect now also cause a crash, type immunity does not. Gen 3 - 1/2 of the damage it would have dealt (at least 1 HP), capped at half of your Pokémon's max HP; type immunity still causes no crash. Gen 4 - the same capped formula on a miss or against Protect, and it now also crashes when your Pokémon is immune (Ghost-type), for half of your Pokémon's max HP. Bulbapedia's Crash damage page gives half of the target's max HP for every Gen 4 crash, but the Platinum decompilation and Pokémon Showdown both use the capped formula. Gen 5-7 - always half of the user's own max HP (rounded down) on a miss, Protect or immunity. Cannot be selected from Gen 8 on.
moves.counter: Never use Protect or Detect, evasion boosts or accuracy drops against it, and from Gen 4 never lead with a Ghost-type (the immunity makes it crash). From Gen 5 a crash costs half its max HP, so keep it above half HP, or asleep, while it can still attack. Gravity (Gen 4+) stops the move being used.

moves.name: High Jump Kick
moves.reason: When the kick fails to land the wild Pokémon crashes and damages itself, which is fatal once it is weakened.
moves.detail: 90% accuracy. Crash damage on a miss: Gen 1 - 1 HP. Gen 2 - 1/8 of the damage the kick would have dealt; Protect/Detect now also cause a crash, type immunity does not. Gen 3 - 1/2 of the damage it would have dealt (at least 1 HP), capped at half of your Pokémon's max HP; type immunity still causes no crash. Gen 4 - the same capped formula on a miss or against Protect, and it now also crashes when your Pokémon is immune (Ghost-type), for half of your Pokémon's max HP. Bulbapedia's Crash damage page gives half of the target's max HP for every Gen 4 crash, but the Platinum decompilation and Pokémon Showdown both use the capped formula. Gen 5+ - always half of the user's own max HP (rounded down) on a miss, Protect or immunity.
moves.counter: Never use Protect or Detect, evasion boosts or accuracy drops against it, and from Gen 4 never lead with a Ghost-type (the immunity makes it crash). From Gen 5 a crash costs half its max HP, so keep it above half HP, or asleep, while it can still attack. Gravity (Gen 4+) stops the move being used.

moves.name: Axe Kick
moves.reason: When the kick fails to land the wild Pokémon crashes for half of its maximum HP, which is fatal at half HP or below.
moves.detail: 90% accuracy. Crash damage: half of the user's max HP if the move misses, is blocked by a protection move, or your Pokémon is immune (Ghost-type). It also has a 30% chance to confuse your Pokémon.
moves.counter: Do not use Protect, evasion boosts or a Ghost-type lead. Keep it above half HP, or asleep, while it can still attack.

moves.name: Supercell Slam
moves.reason: When the slam fails to land the wild Pokémon crashes for half of its maximum HP, which is fatal at half HP or below.
moves.detail: 95% accuracy. Crash damage: half of the user's max HP (rounded down) on a miss; Protect and immunity by type (Ground) or Ability (such as Volt Absorb) count as a miss.
moves.counter: Do not use Protect, evasion boosts, a Ground-type lead or an Electric-absorbing Ability. Keep it above half HP, or asleep, while it can still attack.

moves.name: Curse
moves.reason: A Ghost-type wild Pokémon pays half of its maximum HP to curse your Pokémon, and faints if it has half of its HP or less.
moves.detail: Ghost-type users lose 1/2 of their max HP (rounded down); if that brings them to 0 HP the move still executes and the user faints. Your cursed Pokémon then loses 1/4 of its max HP at the end of each turn until it switches out. Not blocked by Protect. The user pays nothing if Curse fails because your active Pokémon is already cursed. The user's current type decides the effect: non-Ghost users only get -1 Speed, +1 Attack and +1 Defense, which is harmless.
moves.counter: Keep a Ghost-type target above half HP until it is asleep (sleep first, False Swipe second) or Taunt it (Gen 3+, Curse is a status move). Switch your cursed Pokémon out to shed the curse.

moves.name: Mind Blown
moves.reason: The wild Pokémon loses half of its maximum HP every time it uses the move, and faints if it has half of its HP or less.
moves.detail: The user loses 1/2 of its max HP (rounded up) even if the move misses, is blocked by Protect or hits a Substitute. Fails, with no HP lost, while a Pokémon with Damp is on the field. Introduced in Ultra Sun / Ultra Moon; cannot be selected in Brilliant Diamond / Shining Pearl or in Gen 9.
moves.counter: Lead with a Damp Pokémon (the move fails and costs nothing). Otherwise never let it drop to half HP or below while it is awake.

moves.name: Steel Beam
moves.reason: The wild Pokémon loses half of its maximum HP every time it uses the move, and faints if it has half of its HP or less.
moves.detail: The user loses 1/2 of its max HP (rounded up) even if the move misses, is blocked by Protect or hits a Substitute. 95% accuracy. Cannot be selected in Brilliant Diamond / Shining Pearl. Legends: Arceus: the cost is 50% of max HP (33% agile style, 66% strong style).
moves.counter: Never let it drop to half HP or below while it is awake: put it to sleep before weakening it, or catch it at high HP.

moves.name: Chloroblast
moves.reason: The wild Pokémon loses half of its maximum HP when it uses the move, and faints if it has half of its HP or less.
moves.detail: Legends: Arceus: the user loses 50% of its max HP (33% agile style, 66% strong style). Scarlet/Violet: the user loses 1/2 of its max HP (rounded up), but only if the move hits; a miss or Protect costs it nothing. 95% accuracy.
moves.counter: Never let it drop to half HP or below while it is awake: put it to sleep before weakening it, or catch it at high HP. In Scarlet/Violet a Protect on the turn it attacks means no HP is lost.

moves.name: Belly Drum
moves.reason: The wild Pokémon spends half of its maximum HP to max out its Attack, leaving it close to fainting from any later recoil, weather or confusion damage and hitting your catcher far harder.
moves.detail: Costs 1/2 of max HP (rounded down) and sets Attack to +6. It fails, at no cost, unless the user has more than half of its max HP left (the Gen 2 and Gen 3 disassemblies and Pokémon Showdown all fail it at exactly half; Bulbapedia words the threshold as less than half), so it can never faint the user on its own. Gen 2 handheld games: used below 50% HP it still raises Attack by 2 stages through a bug.
moves.counter: Treat it as a free weakening, then avoid further chip damage: skip False Swipe if the target also knows a recoil or crash move, and bring a physically bulky catcher. Taunt blocks it (status move).

moves.name: Substitute
moves.reason: The wild Pokémon spends a quarter of its maximum HP on a decoy that blocks your status moves, wearing itself down each time the decoy is rebuilt.
moves.detail: Costs 1/4 of max HP (rounded down). Gen 2+: fails unless the user has more than 1/4 of its HP left, so it cannot faint itself. Gen 1 handheld games only: a user at exactly 1/4 of its HP makes the Substitute and faints. While the decoy stands, many status moves (sleep, paralysis) fail against it.
moves.counter: Break the decoy before trying to inflict sleep or paralysis, and in Gen 1 do not leave the target at exactly a quarter of its HP.

moves.name: Clangorous Soul
moves.reason: The wild Pokémon spends a third of its maximum HP to raise all of its stats, shrinking its HP buffer while it hits your catcher harder.
moves.detail: Costs 1/3 of max HP and raises Attack, Defense, Sp. Atk, Sp. Def and Speed by one stage each. Fails if the user has 1/3 of its HP or less, so it cannot faint itself. Sound-based status move. Cannot be selected in Brilliant Diamond / Shining Pearl.
moves.counter: Taunt blocks it (status move). Otherwise treat it as a free weakening and avoid adding chip damage on top.

moves.name: Fillet Away
moves.reason: The wild Pokémon spends half of its maximum HP to sharply raise its offences and Speed, shrinking its HP buffer while it hits your catcher harder.
moves.detail: Costs 1/2 of max HP (rounded down) and raises Attack, Sp. Atk and Speed by two stages each. Fails if the user has half of its HP or less, so it cannot faint itself.
moves.counter: Taunt blocks it (status move). Otherwise treat it as a free weakening and avoid adding chip damage on top.

moves.name: Thrash
moves.reason: After its rampage the wild Pokémon becomes confused and can knock itself out by hitting itself.
moves.detail: The user is locked into the move for 2-3 turns (3-4 turns in Gen 1) and then becomes confused. A confused Pokémon may hit itself instead of acting (a typeless 40-power physical hit): 50% chance each turn in Gen 1-6, 33% from Gen 7. Gen 5+: the rampage ends early if the move misses or is blocked, and the user still becomes confused if that happens on what would have been the final turn. A sleeping Pokémon does not hurt itself in confusion.
moves.counter: Catch it or put it to sleep while it is still locked into the rampage, and do not bring it to 1 HP beforehand. Once it is confused and weakened, put it to sleep at once.

moves.name: Petal Dance
moves.reason: After its rampage the wild Pokémon becomes confused and can knock itself out by hitting itself.
moves.detail: The user is locked into the move for 2-3 turns (3-4 turns in Gen 1) and then becomes confused. A confused Pokémon may hit itself instead of acting (a typeless 40-power physical hit): 50% chance each turn in Gen 1-6, 33% from Gen 7. Gen 5+: the rampage ends early if the move misses or is blocked, and the user still becomes confused if that happens on what would have been the final turn. Legends: Arceus: single-turn move, no confusion.
moves.counter: Catch it or put it to sleep while it is still locked into the rampage, and do not bring it to 1 HP beforehand. Once it is confused and weakened, put it to sleep at once.

moves.name: Outrage
moves.reason: After its rampage the wild Pokémon becomes confused and can knock itself out by hitting itself.
moves.detail: The user is locked into the move for 2-3 turns and then becomes confused. A confused Pokémon may hit itself instead of acting (a typeless 40-power physical hit): 50% chance each turn in Gen 2-6, 33% from Gen 7. Gen 5+: the rampage ends early if the move misses, is blocked or your Pokémon is immune, and the user still becomes confused if that happens on what would have been the final turn. Legends: Arceus: single-turn move, no confusion.
moves.counter: Catch it or put it to sleep while it is still locked into the rampage, and do not bring it to 1 HP beforehand. Once it is confused and weakened, put it to sleep at once.

moves.name: Raging Fury
moves.reason: After its rampage the wild Pokémon becomes confused and can knock itself out by hitting itself.
moves.detail: Gen 9: the user is locked into the move for 2-3 turns and then becomes confused (33% chance each turn to hit itself with a typeless 40-power physical hit). The rampage ends early if the move misses, is blocked or your Pokémon is immune, and the user still becomes confused if that happens on what would have been the final turn. In Legends: Arceus (Gen 8) the move only fixates the user and causes no confusion.
moves.counter: Catch it or put it to sleep while it is still locked into the rampage, and do not bring it to 1 HP beforehand. Once it is confused and weakened, put it to sleep at once.

moves.name: Sandstorm
moves.reason: The sandstorm it summons damages every Pokémon that is not Rock-, Ground- or Steel-type at the end of each turn, so a non-immune wild Pokémon left at 1 HP faints.
moves.detail: Lasts 5 turns (8 if the user holds a Smooth Rock, Gen 4+). End-of-turn damage: 1/8 of max HP in Gen 2, 1/16 from Gen 3. Immune: Rock-, Ground- and Steel-types, the Abilities Sand Veil, Sand Rush, Sand Force and Overcoat, and Pokémon with Magic Guard. Your own non-immune Pokémon take the same damage.
moves.counter: Check the target's type and Ability first: if it is immune there is no risk. If it is not, wait out the five turns before weakening it, replace the weather with your own (Rain Dance, Sunny Day), or lead with Cloud Nine to switch weather effects off.

moves.name: Hail
moves.reason: The hailstorm it summons damages every Pokémon that is not Ice-type or shielded by an Ability at the end of each turn, so a non-immune wild Pokémon left at 1 HP faints.
moves.detail: Lasts 5 turns (8 if the user holds an Icy Rock, Gen 4+). Every Pokémon that is not Ice-type loses 1/16 of its max HP at the end of each turn; Pokémon with Ice Body, Snow Cloak, Overcoat or Magic Guard take no hail damage. Cannot be selected in Gen 9, where Snowscape replaces it and deals no damage.
moves.counter: No risk if the target is Ice-type or has Ice Body, Snow Cloak, Overcoat or Magic Guard. Otherwise wait out the five turns before weakening it, replace the weather with your own (Rain Dance, Sunny Day), or lead with Cloud Nine to switch weather effects off.

moves.name: Earthquake
moves.reason: In horde, SOS and double wild battles it hits every adjacent Pokémon, so the shiny's partners can knock it out.
moves.detail: Targets all adjacent Pokémon, allies included. Relevant only while more than one wild Pokémon is on the field; a Flying-type or Levitate shiny is immune.
moves.counter: Knock out the non-shiny Pokémon first with single-target moves; you cannot throw a ball until only one wild Pokémon is left.

moves.reason: In horde, SOS and double wild battles it confuses every adjacent Pokémon, partners included, so a weakened shiny partner can knock itself out in confusion.
moves.detail: Confuses all Pokémon adjacent to the user. A confused Pokémon may hit itself instead of acting (a typeless 40-power physical hit): 50% chance each turn up to Gen 6, 33% from Gen 7. Relevant to the wild side only while more than one wild Pokémon is on the field.
moves.counter: Knock out the non-shiny Pokémon first, and do not weaken the shiny while it is confused; a sleeping Pokémon does not hurt itself in confusion.

moves.name: Mean Look
moves.reason: Your active Pokémon can no longer switch out or run, so you cannot bring in your catcher and are stuck through Perish Song, Curse or Destiny Bond.
moves.detail: Lasts while the wild user stays in battle. From Gen 3 a Pokémon with Run Away or a Smoke Ball can still flee (but not switch). Pivot moves still switch you out: Baton Pass, U-turn (Gen 4+), Volt Switch (Gen 5+), Parting Shot and Flip Turn. Gen 6+: Ghost-types are immune.
moves.counter: Lead with the Pokémon you intend to catch with, or with a Ghost-type (Gen 6+), and carry a pivot move such as U-turn or Volt Switch.

moves.name: Fly
moves.reason: While the wild Pokémon is up in the air you cannot throw a Poké Ball at it, which burns a turn of any Perish Song, weather or PP timer.
moves.detail: Two-turn move with a semi-invulnerable first turn. From Gen 4, Poké Balls cannot be used while the wild Pokémon is in that state (in Gen 1-3 they still work), and most of your moves miss as well. In SOS Battles a Pokémon in this state does not call for help.
moves.counter: Wait for it to come back down, or keep it asleep so it never starts the move.

moves.name: Safeguard
moves.reason: For five turns your catcher cannot put the wild Pokémon to sleep or paralyse it, which stalls a sleep-and-False-Swipe setup while the encounter drags on.
moves.detail: Protects the user's side from non-volatile status conditions and confusion for 5 turns; conditions it already has stay. Gen 4+: removed by Defog. Gen 5+: bypassed by Infiltrator.
moves.counter: Inflict sleep or paralysis before it goes up, or wait five turns. Defog (Gen 4+) clears it and an Infiltrator Pokémon (Gen 5+) ignores it.

moves.name: Metronome
moves.reason: It calls a random move, which can be a self-KO or battle-ending move such as Explosion, Self-Destruct, Memento, Teleport, Roar or Whirlwind.
moves.detail: Bulbapedia's list of moves Metronome cannot call does not include Self-Destruct, Explosion, Misty Explosion, Memento, Final Gambit, Perish Song, Teleport, Roar, Whirlwind, Dragon Tail or Circle Throw in any generation, so every use carries a small chance of ending the encounter. The called move runs at Metronome's normal priority.
moves.counter: A Damp lead neutralises the explosion outcomes. Taunt (Gen 3+, Metronome is a status move) or sleep stops it altogether.

moves.name: Transform
moves.reason: The wild Pokémon becomes a copy of your active Pokémon, so any self-KO, recoil or battle-ending move your lead knows becomes its move too.
moves.detail: Copies the target, including its moves; each copied move has only 5 PP (or its own maximum if lower), so a long fight quickly ends in Struggle.
moves.counter: Lead with a Pokémon that knows no Explosion-type, recoil, crash or Roar / Whirlwind / Teleport moves, and do not stall once it has transformed.
